title: RFID Weapon Tracking Tag — MIL-STD-130N IUID / ATF / NATO Armory Accountability
summary: RFID weapon tracking tags attach a tamper-evident, cryptographically verifiable identifier to every issued firearm, taser, baton, optic and crew-served weapon across military armories, National Guard AA&E vaults, federal law-enforcement evidence rooms, municipal police armories and private security operations. The programme preserves MIL-STD-130N IUID marking, US Army AR 190-11 + AR 710-2 AA&E accountability, Navy OPNAVINST 5530.13D, USMC MCO 5530.14A, USAF AFMAN 31-101, DoD 5200.08-R arms / ammunition / explosives physical security, ATF 27 CFR Part 478 FFL record-keeping, 18 USC §922 GCA, NATO STANAG 2495 + STANAG 4569, NIBIN ballistic correlation, UK Firearms Act 1968, and EU Firearms Directive (EU) 2021/555 marking / tracing obligations.
heroPoints: MIL-STD-130N IUID / DoD UID-compliant per-weapon identifier on each firearm, mapped to the DoD Item Unique Identification Registry, NIIN, DoDAAC and armorer / unit assignment — so AR 190-11 + DoD 5200.08-R + OPNAVINST 5530.13D audits produce a positive-accountability record instead of a clipboard roster.

UHF portal + smart-rack + handheld reader architecture — full armory inventory of 500-5,000 weapons in under 5 minutes instead of the 4-12 hour visual-count process; portal events paired with CAC / PIV / HSPD-12 authenticated identity produce FIPS 201-3 / NIST SP 800-116 chain-of-custody with cryptographic per-scan signatures on NTAG424 DNA variant.

Tamper-evident, firing-validated attachment — potted inside the weapon stock / grip cavity / rail-recess; passes MIL-STD-810H vibration, shock, temperature and altitude profiles; weapon function and accuracy unaffected; tamper-flag (Monza R6-P) + NTAG424 DNA SUN CMAC AES-128 signature flags removal attempts for 18 USC §922 / ATF investigation.
imageAlt: RFID weapon tracking tag installed in a firearm stock cavity for MIL-STD-130N IUID accountability, ATF 27 CFR 478 FFL records and armory portal chain-of-custody

brief.label: Chip options
brief.text: Impinj Monza R6-P (96-bit EPC + 32-bit TID + 64-bit user + 32-bit tamper flag) for primary armory fleets; Impinj M750 / M770 / M775 for long-range rack-level reads; NXP UCODE 9 / 9xe for extended user-memory carrying unit-assignment and armorer service record on the tag; Alien Higgs-9 for portal-wide crowd flow. NTAG424 DNA (13.56 MHz HF) with SUN CMAC AES-128 per-tap signature for federal law-enforcement evidence rooms, NATO Tier-1 armories and ATF FFL inspections requiring tamper-evident per-scan authentication under FIPS 201-3 / NIST SP 800-116 / CJIS Security Policy v5.9.3.

brief.label: Frequency / air interface
brief.text: 860-960 MHz UHF Gen2v2 per EPCglobal Class 1 Gen 2 v2.1 + ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 for portal, rack and handheld reads. 13.56 MHz HF per ISO/IEC 14443-3 Type A + NFC Forum Type 4 Tag Operation v3.0 for NTAG424 DNA per-weapon forensic-tap. ATEX / IECEx Zone 1 / 2 + UL / CSA Class I Div 1 / Div 2 hazardous-area reader stack for ammunition / explosive-atmosphere-adjacent vaults. FCC Part 15 / ETSI EN 302 208 / IC RSS-247 spectrum compliance.

brief.label: Asset identifier scheme
brief.text: DoD UID / IUID per MIL-STD-130N §6 encoded as a GS1 GIAI-96 per GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0 §7.1 (IUID Construct #2: EID / IAC / PNO / SEQ). Carries NSN / NIIN, manufacturer CAGE code, weapon serial (OEM), DoD Property Number / USMC SerTrak ID / USAF Small Arms / USA PS&E, caliber (NATO 9×19 / 5.56×45 / 7.62×51 / 12.7×99 BMG / 40mm MK19 / 12-gauge / Taser 25 / OC baton), fire-control group (FCG) serial where applicable, receiver serial for federal FFL records, and last ATF 27 CFR §478.125 bound-book entry reference. Armory events published as EPCIS 2.0 ObjectEvents with bizStep=issuing / returning / inspecting / transferring / destroying and disposition keyed to AA&E custody state.

brief.label: Form-factor SKUs (6)
brief.text: (1) Stock-cavity potted: 10 × 5 × 2 mm miniature inlay potted in 3M DP-110 / Loctite EA 9460 vibration-dampening compound inside M4 / M16 / M14 / Mk18 / HK416 / SCAR stock cavity or AR-pistol buffer-tube void; (2) Grip-cavity insert: 15 × 8 mm inlay into M9 / M17 / M18 / Glock 17/19/19M / SIG P320 grip panel / M500 stock screw void; (3) Picatinny / M-LOK rail-recess: 20 × 10 mm on-metal on-tag under the existing rail cover, anti-metal Monza R6-P; (4) Receiver etch-pad: 25 × 12 mm discrete on-metal patch under lower-receiver or optic-mount plate for M240 / M2 / Mk19 crew-served fit; (5) Optic / PEQ-15 / PVS-14 accessory tag: 15 × 10 mm on-metal for IUID-tagged ancillary items under MIL-STD-130N §5.3; (6) Gun-case / rifle-rack tag: 40 × 20 mm for storage-level accountability on Pelican / Hardigg / SKB cases and Argos / Space Plus Combat Weapon Rack positions.

brief.label: Environmental qualification
brief.text: MIL-STD-810H Methods 501 / 502 (high/low temperature -40 °C to +85 °C), Method 507 humidity, Method 514 vibration including Annex C Procedure I firing profile, Method 516 shock (40g / 11 ms half-sine) including gun-firing shock, Method 509 salt fog, Method 510 sand/dust, Method 520 combined environments, Method 519 gunfire vibration. 10,000+ round firing qualification across 9×19 / 5.56 / 7.62 / 12-gauge / .50 BMG validated per MIL-STD-810H §514.8 Annex C Procedure I ballistic-shock profile. IP67 / IP68 for field / maritime deployment.

brief.label: Read range
brief.text: 1-3 m handheld at weapon-by-weapon inspection; 2-5 m rack-face scan at the armory rack front; 3-7 m portal read at armory door / evidence-room threshold with CAC / PIV pairing; 0-5 cm HF NFC tap for NTAG424 DNA per-weapon forensic chain-of-custody; 0-10 cm buried-in-stock UHF read via contact-coupled handheld for MIL-SPEC audit where open-air read is blocked.

brief.label: Tamper & physical-security features
brief.text: Monza R6-P 32-bit tamper flag triggers on adhesive / mechanical separation; NTAG424 DNA SUN CMAC AES-128 signs each forensic tap so tag swap or cloning produces a distinct cryptographic mismatch; epoxy potting per 3M DP-110 / Loctite EA 9460 meets US Army DA PAM 710-2-1 tamper-evidence expectation; rail-recess variant carries frangible backing so removal destroys antenna. Event log captures tamper state against the weapon's DoD UID and the armorer's CAC / PIV identity.

sections.title: Why manual weapons accountability fails AR 190-11 + ATF FFL audit
bullets: AR 190-11 physical-security programmes require sensitive-item accountability with positive hand-receipt control; a 500-5,000-weapon armory running visual serial-number counts generates the single largest class of DoD DCSA physical-security-inspection finding, and shift-change inventory often exceeds the time-on-task commanders can reasonably sustain.

DoD Instruction 8320.04 mandates MIL-STD-130N IUID marking for sensitive materiel including small arms; manual roster reconciliation against the DoD IUID Registry is error-prone and creates Registry-vs-field divergence that the DCSA audit scrubs every inspection cycle.

ATF 27 CFR §478.125 bound-book entries for every firearm received / disposed at FFL-holding law-enforcement agencies are routinely reconciled by hand — typos, missed entries and illegible handwriting trigger ATF compliance-inspection violations under §478.123 / §478.125.

NIBIN (FBI / ATF National Integrated Ballistic Information Network) correlation and EU 2021/555 / UN Firearms Protocol tracing require the weapon serial to be demonstrably tied to the recovered ballistic or crime-gun record; paper-log chain-of-custody cannot reliably defend the time-sequenced custody path.

Municipal and private security armories running 100-1,000 weapons with paper sign-out books cannot meet insurance-carrier and CJIS-adjacent evidentiary expectations; weapon loss / theft events reveal log gaps that convert into civil liability and regulatory exposure.

sections.title: Field operating notes — military / law-enforcement armory estates
bullets: Pattern begins with a DoD IUID Registry extract (or FFL bound-book export / municipal armory roster) reconciliation, followed by NSN / NIIN / CAGE-code verification and a GS1 GIAI-96 issuer-code registration before any tag is cut; AA&E risk category assignment (I / II / III / IV per DoD 5200.08-R) sets the hardening profile.

SKU selection balances weapon platform (M4 / M16 / M14 / HK416 / SCAR / M9 / M17 / M18 / Glock / M240 / M2 / Mk19 / PEQ-15 / PVS-14), mounting cavity (stock / grip / rail / receiver / optic / case) and threat profile (barracks / vault / vehicle / field / combat load); MIL-STD-810H Method 514 firing profile is selected per caliber; Method 519 gunfire vibration overlay is selected for crew-served weapons.

Pilot armory: one battalion vault / one precinct armory / one federal FFL holder's evidence room runs the full MIL-STD-130N IUID-encoded programme under portal + smart-rack + handheld for 90 days in parallel with the legacy paper programme; DCSA / ATF / NATO / CJIS audit rehearsal validates the event export and §478.125 bound-book generation.

Enterprise-wide cutover: DoD IUID Registry sync via PIEE / iRAPT; PBUSE / GCSS-Army / AFILS / SerTrak / WAMS feed activation; NIBIN + BRASSTRAX / EVOFINDER ballistic correlation wiring; evidence-room platforms (BEAST / Tracker / FileOnQ / CrimePad) onboarded; EU sites add EUROPOL SIENA / SIS II / iARMS / EWAP and EU 2021/555 tracing export.

faq.question: Does the tag affect weapon function, accuracy or firing shock tolerance?
faq.answer: No. The tag is passive (no battery, no emissions), under 1 gram, and mounted in a non-functional void — stock cavity, grip panel, rail recess, receiver etch-pad. It does not contact moving parts, barrel, chamber or sighting surface. Hardware is qualified under MIL-STD-810H Method 514 Annex C Procedure I gun-firing vibration profile and Method 519 gunfire vibration; 10,000+ rounds across 9×19, 5.56, 7.62, 12-gauge and .50 BMG platforms validated. Tagged weapons pass standard function and accuracy checks without measurable change.

faq.question: How does the programme satisfy MIL-STD-130N IUID and AR 190-11?
faq.answer: Each weapon carries a DoD UID / IUID encoded per MIL-STD-130N §6 under IUID Construct #2 (EID / IAC / PNO / SEQ) on a GS1 GIAI-96 carrier. The tag writes to the DoD IUID Registry via PIEE / iRAPT and syncs to PBUSE / GCSS-Army / AFILS / SerTrak / WAMS depending on service. AR 190-11 physical-security positive accountability is produced by the portal + smart-rack + handheld event stream paired with CAC / PIV / HSPD-12 authenticated identity — DCSA physical-security inspections resolve against the per-weapon record.

faq.question: How does the programme integrate with ATF FFL §478.125 bound-book and NIBIN?
faq.answer: The EPCIS 2.0 event feed auto-generates the ATF 27 CFR §478.125 bound-book entries for every receipt, disposition, transfer, sale and destruction at FFL-holding law-enforcement agencies; ATF eForm / FFL eZ Check export is on-demand. NIBIN ballistic correlation (ATF / FBI) and crime-gun traces resolve to the per-weapon IUID record, closing the evidentiary gap paper logs cannot defend. EU sites export to EUROPOL SIENA / SIS II / iARMS / EWAP and EU 2021/555 tracing.

faq.question: What tamper and anti-clone features are available?
faq.answer: Monza R6-P variant carries a 32-bit tamper flag that triggers on adhesive or mechanical separation. The NTAG424 DNA variant adds SUN CMAC AES-128 per-scan signatures (per NXP AN12196) so each forensic tap produces a distinct cryptographic mismatch if the tag is cloned or swapped. Epoxy potting per 3M DP-110 / Loctite EA 9460 meets DA PAM 710-2-1 tamper-evidence expectation. Rail-recess variants use a frangible backing that destroys the antenna on removal. All events record against the armorer / evidence-custodian's CAC / PIV identity.
